Building a continuously updated manual

Source: vignettes/building-a-continuously-updated-manual.Rmd
building-a-continuously-updated-manual.Rmd

A manual either pins the modules it documents or tracks them, and that choice determines the rest of its setup.

A project manual documents the modules as a particular project used them, so it pins them and the manual agrees with the results it describes. See vignette("building-a-project-manual"); LandWeb is the example.

A continuously updated manual documents the modules as they are now, so it tracks them and a documentation fix reaches the published site without anyone republishing the manual. This vignette covers that arrangement, as used by LandR-Manual and fireSenseManual.

A git submodule records a commit, so keeping it current means someone bumping a pointer for every module change. Checking the modules out by branch in CI records the branch instead, and each build resolves it to whatever that branch points at that day.

Setting one up means a repository holding the book, a workflow that fetches the modules and deploys the rendered site, a build script that assembles the chapters and bibliography, and – if the manual has releases – an archive of released PDFs.

The shape

The manual is its own repository, and the module sources are build output:

<manual>/
  index.Rmd
  _bookdown.yml
  _output.yml
  build.R
  install.R
  DESCRIPTION            # so install.R can resolve the manual's own deps
  modules/               # fetched by CI; gitignored
  _manual_rmds/          # generated chapters; gitignored
  docs/                  # rendered output, deployed to the published branch (gh-pages)
  .github/workflows/

Fetching the modules

Check each module out by branch, with the standard action. The workflow is then the manifest: every entry names a repository and a ref, and there is no custom code to maintain.

env:
  ## one edit moves every module; workflow_dispatch can override it for a trial
  MODULE_REF: development

jobs:
  build-manual-site:
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          repository: PredictiveEcology/Biomass_core
          ref: ${{ github.event.inputs.module_ref || env.MODULE_REF }}
          path: modules/Biomass_core

Use github.event.inputs, not the inputs context, so the expression is null rather than an error on push and schedule events.

A module whose branches differ from the rest can override the default in its own step – but prefer fixing the module. Biomass_validationKNN was checked out at main for a year because work there had resumed directly on main, leaving its development 12 commits behind; the exception then had to be remembered every time MODULE_REF was considered. Merging main back into development let the exception go, and MODULE_REF covers every module again.

Nothing detects the situation that made the exception necessary: a module whose development has quietly fallen behind its main builds perfectly, from stale sources.

Because nothing in the repository records which commits a build used, have the workflow write them out:

      - name: Record module versions
        run: |
          for d in modules/*/; do
            echo "$(basename "$d") $(git -C "$d" rev-parse --short HEAD)"
          done >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

Installing what the chapters need

The manual’s own dependencies come from its DESCRIPTION. The modules declare their own, which cannot be resolved until the modules are on disk:

remotes::install_deps()
SpaDES.docs::installModulePkgs("modules")

The build script 

paths <- SpaDES.docs::manualPaths()

SpaDES.docs::manualVersion()   # index.Rmd's subtitle reads it from the environment

SpaDES.docs::writePkgBib(file.path(paths$citations, "packages.bib"))
SpaDES.docs::downloadCSL("ecology-letters", paths$citations)

## references.bib is OUTPUT ONLY -- see the note below
SpaDES.docs::collapseModuleBibs(
  modulePath = file.path(paths$prj, "modules"),
  extraBibs = file.path(paths$citations, c("packages.bib", "references_manual.bib")),
  outFile = file.path(paths$citations, "references.bib")
)

chapters <- SpaDES.docs::prepManualRmds("./modules", rebuildCache = FALSE)

SpaDES.docs::renderManual(outputDir = paths$docs, output_format = "all")

## these must be inside the published directory, not at the repository root
SpaDES.docs::stagePagesFiles(paths$docs, cname = "example.predictiveecology.org")

unlink(unique(dirname(chapters)), recursive = TRUE)

Use renderManual() rather than bookdown::render_book() directly. bookdown knits once and then writes each declared format in turn, so the website is already on disk when a later format fails, and letting that failure propagate discards it along with the deploy that would have published it. renderManual() reports the failure as a GitHub Actions warning and still requires the site itself, so a format that cannot be built costs only that format.

Declare the fragile formats last in _output.yml, for the same reason: the formats are written in declaration order and a failure stops the rest, so a PDF in the middle costs the EPUB after it too.

Keep the output bibliography out of its own extraBibs: listing it there merges the file into itself on every build, accumulating RefManageR’s :1-suffixed duplicates of every entry. Put curated entries in a tracked file of their own and treat the assembled one as disposable, which it has to be – citations/ is generated and starts empty on CI.

Deploying

The deploy publishes the contents of the rendered directory to a branch, so anything written at the repository root never reaches the site. .nojekyll and CNAME both have to be inside it, which is what stagePagesFiles() is for.

Writing them at the root appears to work for as long as an earlier deploy left copies behind and the action deploys with clean: false. A branch published for the first time has neither, and the failure is quiet: a green build, and a site that either loses its custom domain or drops the _-prefixed directories bookdown emits.

Caching

Cache the directories bookdown actually writes. With output_dir set it writes knitr’s cache to <book_filename>_cache/ and the figures to <book_filename>_files/, both at the repository root. There is no _bookdown_files directory, and caching a path of that name fails silently – the action warns that the path does not exist and saves nothing, on every build.

      - uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: |
            *_cache
            *_files
          key: bookdown-${{ hashFiles('**/*Rmd') }}
          restore-keys: bookdown-

Cache the R library as well. Installing the SpaDES stack from source dominates the job, and a daily schedule would otherwise pay it every day.

Rebuild cadence

schedule, plus workflow_dispatch, plus push to the manual’s own default branch. A daily rebuild keeps the site within a day of the modules without anyone touching this repository.

Per-push rebuilding, where each module repository notifies the manual, needs a token with write access distributed to every module repository, and it rebuilds a whole book because one typo was fixed. The cost is not worth the freshness.

Releases, and keeping the old PDFs

A manual that tracks a branch has no version of its own: it describes whatever the modules say today. A release is the other build, with pinned refs, a version number, and a PDF that stays available after the site has moved on.

Keep the released PDFs in version control, under archive/pdf/, and publish them with the site rather than leaving them on the published branch. That branch is rebuilt by every deploy, and an old PDF cannot be regenerated from current sources – so it is the one artifact that must not live only there.

paths <- SpaDES.docs::manualPaths()

## after render_book(), and only when a PDF was produced
SpaDES.docs::archiveManualPDF(
  file.path(paths$docs, "MyManual.pdf"),
  version = read.dcf("DESCRIPTION", fields = "Version")[1],
  prefix = "my-manual"
)

## publish every archived release with the site, and index them
SpaDES.docs::publishManualArchive(
  archiveDir = file.path(paths$prj, "archive", "pdf"),
  docsDir = paths$docs,
  manualName = "My Manual"
)

Take the version from DESCRIPTION rather than setting it in the build script. Two places to edit is one place to forget, and archiveManualPDF() refuses an empty version rather than writing my-manual-v.pdf over the previous release.

Link the archive from the book’s preface with a static link to archive/. The page behind it is regenerated every build from the files actually present, so nothing has to be edited when a release is cut.

Committing the new PDF

Have the workflow do it, so a release does not depend on someone remembering:

      ## after the deploy, never before it -- see below
      - name: Archive the release PDF
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          ## '??' is untracked: a version not in the repository before. A
          ## modified tracked file is a re-render of a version already archived
          if [ -z "$(git status --porcelain archive/pdf | grep '^??' || true)" ]; then
            echo "No newly archived PDF; nothing to commit."
            git checkout -- archive/pdf 2>/dev/null || true
            exit 0
          fi
          git checkout -- archive/pdf 2>/dev/null || true
          version="$(Rscript -e 'cat(read.dcf("DESCRIPTION", fields = "Version")[1])')"
          branch="archive/pdf-v${version}"
          if gh pr list --head "${branch}" --state open --json number --jq 'length' \
               | grep -qv '^0$'; then
            echo "A pull request for ${branch} is already open."
            exit 0
          fi
          git config --local user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config --local user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git checkout -b "${branch}"
          git add archive/pdf
          git commit -m "Archive the manual PDF for v${version}"
          git push --force \
            "https://x-access-token:${GH_TOKEN}@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git" \
            "HEAD:refs/heads/${branch}"
          gh pr create --base "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --head "${branch}" \
            --title "Archive the manual PDF for v${version}"

Three parts of that need to stay as they are.

Open a pull request; do not push. A ruleset on the default branch refuses a direct push, with GH006: Changes must be made through a pull request. Note also that the step is gated if: github.event_name != 'pull_request', so no pull request build runs it: whatever it does is first exercised by a merge, and should be read carefully rather than trusted to a green check.

Test for an untracked file, not for any change. A PDF is not reproducible byte for byte – xelatex stamps a creation date and a document ID into each run – so git status --porcelain archive/pdf reports a modification after every build, and a check for any change opens a pull request every night. Requires SpaDES.docs >= 0.5.1, which leaves an already-archived version alone; this check covers the case where something else rewrites the file.

Put it after the deploy. A failure here must not stop the site from updating, which is what happens when it runs first: nothing handling a secondary artifact should be able to withhold the primary one.

Linking the versions

bs4_book has no download menu: download: ["pdf", "epub"] is a gitbook option, accepted and ignored under bookdown::bs4_book, so setting it publishes the files with nothing pointing at them. Link them from the landing page:

## in index.Rmd, in a `results = "asis"` chunk
cat(SpaDES.docs::manualArchiveLinks(manualName = "My Manual"), sep = "")

manualArchiveLinks() lists the archived releases newest first, from the files present, excluding the version being built. For the current build’s own PDF and EPUB, take the formats from _output.yml rather than testing for the files: bs4_book renders first, so neither file exists yet when index.Rmd is knitted, and a test for them drops the links from every build.

Do not use clean-exclude for this

Keeping the archive only on the published branch, preserved with the deploy action’s clean-exclude, looks simpler and is worse. It reintroduces files that linger on that branch without any build producing them – which is how a stale PDF from a previous era ends up published beside a current one. Deploying with clean: true, from a directory the build fully populates, keeps the branch an exact image of what was built.

Adding a module

Three things change together, and two of them fail quietly:

  1. a checkout step in the workflow;
  2. a chapter entry in _bookdown.yml;
  3. the module list in the manual’s landing page, if it has one.

Miss the second and the chapter is fetched, staged and silently absent from the book. prepManualRmds() warns in both directions for this reason. Miss the third and it is in the book but not on the landing page, which nothing checks.
